RagShortTexts: Roman frontier posts needed garrisons, patrols, repairs and provisions to guard crossings.

Variants.Content: Garrisons along the Rhine and Danube held forts, patrolled roads and watched crossings. Posts protected routes and stores, but long riverbanks, forests and tributaries offered concealed approaches. Repairs, grain storage and contact with nearby units formed everyday frontier work.

Patrols identified roads, water levels and possible landing places and reported locations and directions. Winter, floods and darkness changed passage. Shelter behind walls did not ensure rations; men still needed footwear, clothing and delivered food.

Fort construction required craftsmen, materials, transport and garrisons. Spreading troops among too many posts weakened each, while failed supply could force men to seek food away from duty. Frontier defense also needed mobile support.
